abstraction_design.rationale: The good abstractions (card component, memo loader, model types) stretch to the Items scenario for data, but page-level section markup is copy-pasted across routes and the ability loader duplicates the card-mapping helper with a hand-rolled variation.

findings.issue: Card sprites are built from a hardcoded URL pattern (/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png) instead of the API-provided sprites.front_default, baking the media layout into the app and making the Deoxys-style default-Pokémon fix require new per-Pokémon fetch plumbing.
findings.suggestion: Thread the default Pokémon's front_default through cardFromSpecies (fetch via the memoized getPokemon), keeping spriteForId as a fallback.

findings.issue: loadAbilityPage duplicates the ref-to-card mapping in cardsFromPokemonRefs (id>10000 filter, speciesById lookup, dedupe) with only a hidden-flag merge as variation.
findings.suggestion: Reuse cardsFromPokemonRefs for the card list and apply hidden flags in a second pass, or extend the helper with an optional ref-decorator.

findings.issue: Page-section scaffolding (fact-list dl, Effect panel, '<count> Pokémon' + card list) is inlined and duplicated across moves, abilities and types routes, so any similarly-shaped new section (e.g. Items) is copy-paste.
findings.suggestion: Lift a Panel/FactList and a PokemonCardSection component and compose routes from them.

findings.issue: The link-flavoured type badge (className `type-badge type-${name}`) is re-inlined in four places while a non-link TypePill already exists in PokemonCard.tsx.
findings.suggestion: Add a TypeBadgeLink component (or an asChild/as prop on TypePill) and use it everywhere.

findings.issue: PokemonPageData (and all page types) carry unused fields — found, speciesName, sprite — never read by any route component (null return already signals not-found).
findings.suggestion: Drop the unused fields or use them, so model types stay an honest contract.

findings.issue: Knowledge of the home query params is split across three helpers (validateSearch, updateSearch, pageSearch), so adding or renaming a filter touches all three and they can drift.
findings.suggestion: Build pageSearch/updateSearch from the same canonical param list (a single keys array or a shared helper) as validateSearch.

findings.issue: The #moves anchor scroll is a manual useEffect/requestAnimationFrame DOM reach-around inside the route component.
findings.suggestion: Rely on the browser's native hash behavior (the section has id="moves") or centralize hash scrolling in the router's scrollRestoration config.

findings.issue: Every keystroke navigates (replace) with no debounce, triggering a server-fn round trip per character; the spec explicitly allows 300 ms debouncing.
findings.suggestion: Debounce the navigate call so future edits to filtering don't inherit a request-per-keystroke pattern.

summary: This is a well-seamed, current-stable TanStack Start app: idiomatic server/client separation (.server.ts + createServerFn .validator() wrappers), a single data-access layer that owns the API base URL and caching, and one shared card component behind every Pokémon list, so most data bugs and data-source changes land in one obvious file. Weaknesses are copy-paste at the edges — duplicated section markup across routes, a re-implemented card helper in the ability loader, and repeated type-badge markup — which is exactly what an Items-style extension would trip over. Overall this is code a team can change confidently, with modest refactoring needed before the next similar feature.
